text.p: Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Sunday he had found injustice everywhere in Pakistan and vowed his six-month-old government would reform the society with people's help.
Speaking to a public rally at the graveside of late military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq beside Islamabad's huge Faisal mosque, he also said he wanted quick punishment of criminals.
The rally of thousands of people marked the ninth anniversary of General Zia's death in a mysterious plane crash.
"I go to places and I see injustice everywhere," said Sharif, a one-time protege of Zia.
"It hurts my heart to see there is so much oppression, people have so many problems.

"I wish there were such a system of justice...in accordance with the Sharia (Islamic law) under which anybody committing a crime is punished the same night," said Sharif, who has been sharply criticised for a recent law he brought in that gives sweeping powers to police and only a week to an anti-terrorist court to decide a case.
Sharif says the law, passed by parliament last week, was necessary to fight a current wave of Moslem sectarian violence in his home province of Punjab and ethnic violence in the port city of Karachi.
But opposition parties, some lawyers' associations and human rights groups have voiced fears that it could be misused by police and could target the government's political opponents.

"There is unemployment here, there is illiteracy here, there is poverty in Pakistan, there are problems in villages, there are problems in cities, there are social vices," Sharif said in his speech. "We have to fix them all."
He said he was sure people would "march in one step with us and make Pakistan a respectable and honourable society".
Many of Sharif's political colleagues are one-time followers of Zia, who seized power in a 1977 bloodless military coup that toppled then prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
Zia, who hanged Bhutto after a controversial conspiracy-to-murder conviction, was himself killed in a mysterious plane crash on August 17, 1988.
An official inquiry at the time concluded the crash of Zia's C-130 military transport in the desert near the Punjab province town of Bahawalpur was probably caused by sabotage, but did not say how.
